name: Biological Pathways
description: Lecture: biological pathways: metabolic, genetic and signaling pathways; introduction to energy metabolism; metabolic repercussions: reactive oxygen species and antioxidant defense pathways.; metabolic disorders- diabetes and beyond; general principles of signal transduction- types of signals, secondary messengers and signal amplification; extracellular signal and role of receptors- cell surface and nuclear receptors, enzymes with kinase activity-receptor tyrosine kinases; signaling proteins can act as molecular switches- adapters and small GTPases; kinases- roles in physiology and pathology, MAPK and phosphatases, sensors of metabolism/stress- AMPK, mTOR and beyond; protein–protein interactions in signal transduction; signaling outcomes; signaling in migration and chemotaxis; regulatory rewiring of metabolism in cancer; small molecule modulators of metabolism. Laboratory: introduction to cell culture- counting, seeding and passaging cells; monitoring of glycolysis in cultured cells- glucose uptake by fluorimetry and lactate production by spectrophotometry, influence of external conditions; monitoring cell death by WST8 viability assays- probing cell death pathways using inhibitors; monitoring stress signaling- effect of kinase inhibitors on MAPK signaling by immunoblot analyses, effect of concentration and time.; cytokine signaling: TNF-induced signal transduction- monitoring signaling kinetics.
